intro: A practical decision framework for mid-handicap golfers choosing a driver without getting trapped by distance claims alone.
disclosure: ArcPoint Gear uses research-based buying guidance and price tiers only when retailer pricing is discussed.

factors.title: Start With Strike
factors.text: Before chasing lower spin, identify where you miss on the face and whether your driver protects ball speed on those strikes.

factors.title: Fit Launch First
factors.text: Loft, shaft profile, and head design should create playable launch and spin, not just the lowest launch-monitor spin number.

factors.title: Control The Miss
factors.text: A driver that narrows dispersion is usually more valuable than one that adds occasional peak distance but widens the bad shot.

sections.heading: Buying Factors
body: Mid-handicap golfers should start with forgiveness, launch window, and dispersion. Most players in this range still miss the center often enough that stability and ball-speed retention are more important than a compact low-spin head.

sections.heading: Loft and Shaft Guidance
body: A 10.5° head is a common starting point, while 12° can help golfers who launch the ball too low. Shaft weight and flex should be fit to tempo, speed, and strike pattern rather than ego.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
body: Common mistakes include choosing a tour head because better players use it, buying for one perfect launch-monitor swing, ignoring face-angle bias, and skipping a basic fitting when spending premium-driver money.

faqs.question: What driver loft is best for mid-handicap golfers?
faqs.answer: Many mid-handicap golfers should test 10.5° first, with 12° worth testing if launch is low or carry distance is weak.

faqs.question: Should mid-handicap golfers prioritize distance or forgiveness?
faqs.answer: Forgiveness and dispersion should usually come first. Extra distance only helps if it stays playable.

faqs.question: Do mid-handicap golfers need a custom fitting?
faqs.answer: A basic fitting is strongly recommended before buying a premium driver because loft, shaft, and face-angle choices can change results dramatically.
